summary: A casual Bangkok Chinese-Thai roast-meat meal: khao na pet (ข้าวหน้าเป็ด) is roast duck over rice with sauce; ba mee pet (บะหมี่เป็ด) pairs it with egg noodles, served in soup or dry. Bang Rak and Yaowarat are useful areas to seek it out.
whyGo: A quick, filling way to try Bangkok’s Chinese-influenced roast-meat cooking, usually with sweet-savory duck sauce and simple accompaniments.
Choose rice for a straightforward plate or egg noodles for a soup or dry noodle variation.
bestFor: A casual lunch or dinner in Bang Rak or Chinatown.
Travelers who enjoy roast meats, egg noodles and rich, slightly sweet sauces.
skipIf: You avoid meat or need a reliably vegetarian meal.
You have strict dietary restrictions or allergies that a small shop cannot confidently confirm; broth, sauces and shared preparation can include other ingredients.
duration: About 30–60 minutes for a simple meal; this is a planning estimate and excludes travel or queues.
cost: Budget roughly ฿60–150 for a simple local plate as a planning estimate: one Bangkok meal report recorded ฿60 in January 2026. A more polished Yaowarat option, Chop Chop Cook Shop, lists roast duck noodle soup at ฿390, or roast duck at ฿320 with rice/noodles as a ฿30 add-on. Confirm menus and prices near the visit.
hours: Hours vary by shop. Current example: Chop Chop Cook Shop at 328 Yaowarat Road lists Tuesday–Sunday, 12:00–22:00, and is closed Monday. Smaller neighborhood shops may sell out or keep different schedules.
bestTime: Go around lunch or early dinner while the roast meats are turning over. For a popular venue, arrive early or reserve; December can be busy, but no dish-specific seasonal event is known.
gettingThere: Pick a specific shop before setting out because the activity is spread across neighborhoods. For the Yaowarat example Chop Chop Cook Shop, use its address at 328 Yaowarat Road, Chakkrawat, Samphanthawong; check a live map from your starting point. Bang Rak choices cluster around Charoen Krung Road.
booking: Most simple roast-duck counters are walk-in. Chop Chop Cook Shop provides online table reservations; booking is sensible for a group or a peak dinner, while solo diners can check availability on arrival.
accessibility: Access varies by shop and sidewalk. Chop Chop’s reservation form accepts wheelchair and stroller accommodation requests, but does not specify step-free access or toilet details; contact the venue to confirm before relying on it.
practicalTips: Ask for ข้าวหน้าเป็ด (khao na pet) for duck with rice, or บะหมี่เป็ด (ba mee pet) for duck with egg noodles. Noodles may be ordered with soup or dry at some shops.
Point to the menu or use the Thai dish name if English is limited; say whether you want soup or dry noodles.
If you avoid pork, ask specifically about the broth, sauces, toppings and shared utensils; roast-meat shops commonly serve pork alongside duck.
Eat soon after serving. Duck skin and sauce can be rich, and the crispness fades as the food sits.
decemberNotes: Bangkok’s December cool season is generally comfortable for walking between food stops, though afternoons remain warm. Check the chosen shop’s holiday hours shortly before going; the listed regular schedule does not confirm Christmas or New Year changes.
uncertainties: This is a dish and neighborhood recommendation rather than one fixed venue; individual shops, prices and hours change.
The ฿60 price is a single reported meal from January 2026, not a representative current price survey.
Chop Chop’s current menu and regular hours are published online, but its December 2026 holiday schedule and detailed accessibility facilities are not confirmed.
